On the first match it returns `len(tokens) - index - 1`, which converts the reversed index back to the original index of the rightmost match. If nothing matches, it raises `ValueError('(token, value) pair not found')`. That is the only absent-pair behavior in the file. Review points: (1) the function needs a list or other sequence, because `reversed()` and `len()` fail on generators; (2) callers must handle or deliberately propagate the ValueError; (3) the slice `[:2]` assumes tokenize tuples. Because the search itself is small and self-contained, I'd keep raw.py short. The remaining time goes to radon/complexity.py and radon/visitors.py. There I'd check for similar scan-and-raise patterns, how ValueError is used (complexity.py:41 raises it for a different reason), and whether any caller depends on this behavior. I'd put most of the time into those two files, then spend a short pass on metrics.py.
